title: open-tennis-robots-ci: the cad job ran 19 min of its 20 min timeout; the next CAD slice will time it out
problem: The cad job runs cad/tests, which builds the collector and the feeder packages fresh (the feeder build does the elevation, azimuth, feed-stroke and cable collision sweeps). On PR #15557 (hopper agitator, 2026-11-13) it took 17:45:19 to 18:04:18 UTC, 19 of the 20 minutes in timeout-minutes. Locally on 4 CPUs the same suite took 27 min and one feeder build 10 min. Every new part adds pairs to the sweeps, so the next slice is likely to hit the timeout and read as a red CI that is only slow. The workflow is under .github/, so the fix waits for the owner (CODEOWNERS).
evidence: PR #15557 check run 'cad': started 2026-11-13T17:45:19Z, completed 2026-11-13T18:04:18Z, success
local: python -m unittest discover -s tests in cad/: Ran 80 tests in 1636.571s, OK
change: Either raise timeout-minutes on the cad job (e.g. to 45), or have the tests build each package once and share it between test_committed_package_is_current and the other package tests (a module-level cache), or split the sweeps into their own job.
metric: cad job wall time on open-tennis-robots PRs

history.note: Fixed in the tests, not the workflow (no control-plane PR): the collector and feeder package builds start as subprocesses in setUpModule and run beside the other tests; the clean-design sweeps the feeder build already runs (elevation, azimuth, feed stroke, cable loop) are asserted once from its manifest instead of re-run by four geometry tests; cable_sweep takes poses/azimuths so the shifted-loop failure case checks 1 pose of 21. Local, 4 CPUs, same machine: 1627 s before, 805 s after, all tests OK. CI wall time not yet measured: compare the cad job on the next open-tennis-robots PR against the 19 min baseline.
